name: RDM6300 125 kHz RFID reader
description: 125 kHz (EM4100-type) read-only RFID card/tag reader. While a tag is in the field it sends the tag's 10-hex-digit ID over a 9600-baud 8N1 TTL UART as a 14-byte frame (0x02, 10 ASCII hex characters, 2 ASCII hex XOR checksum, 0x03). Runs on 5 V +/-5 %, under 50 mA; reads tags at up to about 5 cm. Sold as: RDM6300 125KHz EM4100 RFID reader module (38.5 x 19 mm, P1 TX/RX/-/GND/+5V, P2 ANT1/ANT2 with the supplied coil antenna, P3 LED/+5V/GND).
eli5: Hold a 125 kHz key fob or card near its coil and it tells your board the card's ID number.

pins.name: TX
pins.description: P1 pin 1: UART data out, 9600 baud 8N1, 5 V TTL level (use a divider for 3.3 V GPIOs)

pins.name: RX
pins.description: P1 pin 2: UART data in; the module has no documented commands, leave unconnected

pins.name: ANT1
pins.description: P2 pin 1: antenna coil (the supplied coil is plugged in here)

pins.name: LED
pins.description: P3 pin 1: read indicator LED drive output, optional

pins.name: +5V2
pins.description: P3 pin 2: +5 V (same supply as P1 pin 5), for the indicator LED

pins.name: GND2
pins.description: P3 pin 3: ground (same as P1 pin 4)

buildNotes: Power from 5 V (VBUS/VIN), never 3.3 V: the datasheet allows 5 V +/-5 % only.
TX idles high at the 5 V supply level. On an ESP32 or Pico put a divider (e.g. 1 kOhm series, 2 kOhm to GND) between TX and the GPIO.
Only TX, GND and +5V are needed. RX takes no documented commands; leave it and P3 unconnected.
Keep the antenna coil plugged into P2 and away from metal and the ESP32 antenna; read range is about 5 cm.
Frames repeat while the tag stays in the field; check the XOR checksum and ignore bad frames.

sim.quantity: Tag ID (10 hex digits, as a number)

controls.quantity: Tag held near the coil (1 = yes)

example.code:
from machine import UART, Pin
import time
from rdm6300 import RDM6300

u = UART({UART_ID}, baudrate=9600, bits=8, parity=None, stop=1, rx=Pin({TX}))
reader = RDM6300(u)
print('Waiting for a tag')
while True:
    r = reader.read()
    if r:
        tag, card = r
        print('TAG=%s CARD=%d' % (tag, card))
    time.sleep_ms(50)
